scope: Private checker attached script calls and yield, with Rust execution witnesses. Includes capture effects, lexical block presence, repeated yields, nonlocal control and errors through cleanup. Native block drivers, deeper lexical forwarding and retained-address mutation histories remain incomplete.

cases.source: def once; yield 7; end; def run -> int; once {|x| x}; end
def twice; yield 1; yield 2; end; def run -> int; sum=0; twice {|x| sum+=x}; sum; end
def once; yield; end; def run; x=7; once {|x| x="shadow"}; x+1; end
def ignore; 7; end; def run -> int; ignore {missing}; end
def once; if block_given?; yield 7; else; missing; end; end; def run -> int; once {|x| x}; end
cases.difference: Rust knows the function has an attached block and skips the unreachable no-block branch. Go warns about its missing name.

cases.source: def once; yield; end; def other; once {block_given?}; end; def run; other {7}; end
def once; yield; missing; end; def run; once {break 7}; end
cases.difference: Rust carries break through the yielding function and skips its unreachable tail. Go warns about the tail.

cases.source: def once; yield; missing; end; def run; once {return 7}; missing; end
cases.difference: Rust routes the nonlocal return to the attaching function and skips both unreachable tails. Go warns about both names.

cases.source: def once; yield; end; def run; x=0; result=once {x=7; break 9}; [result,x]; end
def once; yield; end; def run; x=0; begin; once {x=7; return 9}; ensure; return x; end; end
def once; begin; yield; ensure; return 9; end; end; def run; x=0; result=once {x=7; return 2}; [result,x]; end
def once; yield; end; def run; once {begin; break 2; ensure; next 9; end}; end
def repeat; result=while true; yield; end; result; end; def run; repeat {break 7}; end
def repeat; result=while true; yield; end; result; end; def run; repeat {break}; end
def once; yield; end; def run; x=0; begin; once {x=7; raise "bad"}; rescue; x; end; end
def twice; begin; yield 1; rescue; yield 2; end; end; def run; x=0; twice {|n| x+=n; if n==1; raise "bad"; end}; x; end
def once -> int; yield; end; def run; x=0; begin; once {x=7; "bad"}; rescue; x; end; end
cases.difference: Rust propagates the block result to the receiving function return contract and diagnoses its rejected string. Go reports no warning.

cases.source: def once -> int; yield; end; def run; x=0; begin; once {x=7; break "bad"}; rescue; x; end; end
cases.difference: Rust checks a block break value against the receiving function return contract and diagnoses its rejected string. Go reports no warning.

cases.source: def once; yield; end; def run; x=0; once {once {x=7}; x}; x; end
def once; yield; end; def run; a=[]; once {copy=a; copy.push(7)}; a; end
def once; yield; end; def run; x=[]; begin; once {x.push(7); raise "bad"}; rescue ZeroDivisionError; missing; rescue RuntimeError; x; end; end
cases.difference: Rust propagates the specific callback error class and skips the unmatched rescue clause. Go warns about the name in that clause.

cases.source: def twice; yield; yield; end; def run; done=false; result=twice {done=true; break 7}; if done; result; else; missing; end; end
cases.difference: Rust preserves the callback capture write on break and narrows the resulting boolean branch. Go warns about the unreachable name.
